tagline: Over southern California's highest pass, down to the Santa Ana.
intro: Out of Big Bear City, Highway 38 heads southeast and climbs to Onyx Summit. Past the top it turns south and then southwest and begins a slow descent along Cienaga Seca Creek, by the forest road to Heart Bar Campground, to the upper Santa Ana River near the South Fork campground.

On the way down the road looks out over the Sand to Snow National Monument, which runs from about 1,000 feet on the Coachella Valley floor to over 11,000 feet in these mountains. The headwaters of the Santa Ana are inside it.

moments.title: Big Bear City
moments.text: Big Bear takes its name from the grizzlies that once roamed the valley. The post office here opened in 1927 as Van Duesen and became Big Bear City six months later.

moments.title: Onyx Summit
moments.text: At 8,443 feet, the highest mountain pass in southern California, with Onyx Peak standing nearly 700 feet higher beside it.

moments.title: San Gorgonio Mountain
moments.text: The forest road to Heart Bar Campground also leads to a trail up Old Greyback, at 11,503 feet the highest peak in southern California, its summit plateau a square mile across.

practical: The road is open all year, but this country gets snow and chains may be needed in winter.
